description:
docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Part B item B2.

=== DONE (s470bm) ===

SHIPPED
  Pl/Manifest.pm          the collector and the report
  Pl/Passes.pm            set_form_hook / set_text_hook — an OBSERVER of every
                          finished top-level form, and of the two v1-TEXT
                          buckets; return value discarded, so it cannot change
                          emission
  Pl/Parser2.pm           two note_text calls where `captured`/`sched` are built
  pl2cl                   `--manifest`, printing JSON INSTEAD of the CL
  Pl/t/manifest-01.t      43 rows, 1.7 s
  docs/ir-spec.md §10b    normative

THE ONE WALK: `Pl::Passes::run` is where every top-level form passes on its way
to text (Parser2::_lower_sections calls it for decls, defs, run and
pkg_enter), so the collector hangs off the registry's own hook — no second
walk, no second tree representation.  The two buckets that never become trees
(`captured`, `sched`) are regex-scanned instead and the manifest SAYS SO
(`text_scanned`).  With the flag absent nothing is loaded and each site is one
scalar test.  `tools/corpus-diff.pl ee9a658` IDENTICAL over 111 files + 6
shapes, which is the bar that the default emission did not move.

TWO THINGS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, both of which the first version got
wrong:
  * two consecutive `my` STATEMENTS are TWO `p-let` forms, not one form with
    two entries (each nests its block remainder);
  * the `local` family is entirely v1 TEXT and has two shapes —
    `(p-local-cell $g (p-box-for-local 2))` where `p-box-for-local` is the
    VALUE WRAPPER, and `(let (($/ (p-box-for-local ":")))` where it is the
    site's ONLY marker.  Counting both heads gave 6 sites for 5 `local`s;
    counting only `p-local-*` gave 3.  The site count is (p-local-* heads) +
    (p-box-for-local) − (the wraps), and note_text counts the wraps.

THE FOUR-POPULATION MEASUREMENT (scratch/s470bm/manifests/*.summary):

  perl-tests, 111 files, 333 distinct ops used.  Nonzero in the most files:
    phase.eval_when 103, phase.begin 102, regex.qr 58, magic_global_write 56,
    string_eval 55, local 51, regex.literal 51, eval_block 48, io 45.
    ZERO everywhere: formats, phase.check, phase.run_blocks, string_eval.thunk,
    xs.
  lib/**.pm, 22 files, 195 distinct ops.  return 14 files (188 sites) —
    the shims are subs, and `tail-return` fires 128/308, four times the
    corpus's rate.  local only 2 files.
  perl's own t/, 592 files (13 do not transpile), the same shape at scale:
    eval_when 549, begin 468, io 253, regex.literal 240, die 226, qr 221,
    string_eval 205, magic_global_write 202, local 190.  formats appears at
    last — 9 files, 106 sites.
  cpan-tests dist t/, 287 of 289 files.  The one population whose shape
    DIFFERS: string_eval is in only 14 files (18 sites) against half the
    corpus, `goto` and formats are ZERO, and `local` is high (81 files) — real
    CPAN test code is far more portable than perl's own test suite is.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAYS FOR A BACKEND (the question Part B asked): the phase
model and I/O are universal; string eval is in HALF the corpus and a third of
perl's t/, so "no compiler at run time" refuses a very large share; `local`
and magic-global writes are in ~45 % of files, so the save/restore stack is
not optional; `goto` is 5 files, formats 0 in the corpus and 9 in perl's own,
xs 0 everywhere — those three can be refused cheaply.

FACTS, summed over the corpus: raw-slot 196/1898, raw-numeric 41/1898,
str-buffer 2/1898, foreach-raw 53/564, foreach-range 85/564, classic-sort
90/221, elem-setf 85/271, tail-return 63/130, local-push 3/130,
insensitive-call 71/525.

THE DRIFT GUARD: Pl/Manifest.pm's %OBLIGATION is its own data (what machinery
a TARGET needs), deliberately not §10's taxonomy (what an op IS).  A gate row
asserts every op name it mentions exists in docs/ir-op-inventory.tsv, so a
renamed op fails a row instead of silently dropping out of `needs`.

NOT DONE HERE (by the brief): the regex TIER classifier is B5's — the manifest
prints `tier: unclassified`, a DECLARED absence.  B3 (`:needs` per sub) is the
same walk keyed by sub and is a separate item.
